Haisla

Haisla public history connects Kitamaat Village with fishing, oolichan processing, trade and seasonal movement. These starting readings combine the Nation’s historical interpretation with a Haisla–First Nations Education Foundation language resource, distinguishing the broader people, the band government and particular language descriptions.

03

Kitamaat and seasonal livelihoods

Haisla Nation’s history connects the people with Kitamaat Village and surrounding lands and waters. It describes fishing, hunting and trade, giving oolichan oil particular importance as food and an exchange item. Its explanation of the names Kitamaat and Kitimat is expressly grounded in oral history. The account also describes the disruption of seasonal movement and governance under colonial policies. Original records behind those interpretations still need separate inspection.

Read the sources [4] Haisla Nation

04

Language and ways of writing

The Haisla LanguageCloud resource identifies Kitamaat and Kitlope dialects and explains that more than one accurate alphabet has been used to write Haisla. Its chosen transcription is based on an alphabet devised by Emmon Bach. The platform identifies itself as a collaboration between Haisla and the First Nations Education Foundation. This short introduction helps readers approach spelling differences without treating every written variation as a different people or community.

Read the sources [2] Haisla Nation and First Nations Education Foundation
